name: Li Yu
credit: Portrait of Li Yu (Li Houzhu) by Wang Qi, block print from Sancai Tuhui (1609) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Li Yu (937-978) was the last ruler of the Southern T'ang and a celebrated writer of lyrics. Fir-Flower Tablets prints this poem only as the work of "a descendant of the founder of the Southern T'ang dynasty" (circa A.D. 960); the editor identifies the writer as Li Yu, and the date above is the book's own.
The archive holds this one lyric from Fir-Flower Tablets (1921), a poem of separation set in an empty courtyard on an autumn night.

poems.title: Together We Know Happiness
poems.author: Li Yu
poems.note: In the book: "Written by a descendant of the founder of the Southern T'ang dynasty" (circa A.D. 960); the editor identifies the writer as Li Yu, last ruler of the Southern T'ang.
poems.translator: trans. Florence Ayscough and Amy Lowell (1921)
poems.text:
Silent and alone, I ascended the West Cupola.
The moon was like a golden hook.
In the quiet, empty, inner courtyard, the coolness of early Autumn enveloped the wu-t'ung tree.

Scissors cannot cut this thing;
Unravelled, it joins again and clings.
It is the sorrow of separation,
And none other tastes to the heart like this.
